subfield: Condensed matter physics / semiconductor physics of energy materials
motivation: Miyasaka first used metal halide perovskites as photovoltaic absorbers (2009). Park made the first long-term-stable solid-state perovskite cell (2012). Snaith showed that perovskites act as ambipolar semiconductors with long carrier diffusion lengths in planar thin-film devices (2012-2013). Together these results opened a new class of solution-processed semiconductors. Their unusual physics has since been studied intensively: defect tolerance, weak non-radiative recombination despite disorder, and mixed ionic-electronic conduction. This work gave single-junction efficiencies above 26% and perovskite-silicon tandems above 33%, better than any earlier thin-film technology and reached in about a decade. Perovskites have changed how we understand charge generation and transport in soft, disordered semiconductors, and they now point to a realistic path to cheaper, higher-efficiency solar power for decarbonising the global energy system. The discovery has both deep physical content and consequences for society.
